# Tutorial - Adding a Custom Agent

This tutorial adds a real subagent to the harness: subclass `AbstractAgent`, register it on the app, and run a task
through it.
Code: `berg_agents/core/interface.py` (`AbstractAgent`), `berg_agents/app.py` (`register_agent`, `execute`).

## 1. Write the agent class

Every subagent implements two methods: `can_handle(task)` returning a 0--1 confidence, and
`execute(task, context, model)` returning an `AgentResult`.

```python
# my_package/agents/custom_reviewer.py
from typing import Any

from berg_agents.core.interface import AbstractAgent, AgentResult, TaskContext


class CustomReviewer(AbstractAgent):
    """Echoes back the first 100 characters of the task description."""

    name = "custom_reviewer"
    description = "Echo back the first 100 characters of a task"
    preferred_complexity = "trivial"
    capabilities = ["review"]

    def can_handle(self, task: dict[str, Any]) -> float:
        if "review" in task.get("description", "").lower():
            return 0.9
        return 0.1

    def execute(
        self,
        task: dict[str, Any],
        context: TaskContext,
        model: Any = None,
    ) -> AgentResult:
        snippet = task.get("description", "")[:100]
        return AgentResult(success=True, output=f"Review snippet: {snippet}")
```

Check `AgentResult`'s fields in `berg_agents/core/interface.py` before constructing it --- the contract is `success`,
`output`, `error`, `needs_human_review`, `review_reasons`, `model_used`, `tokens_used`, `metadata`.

## 2. Register it on the app

```python
from berg_agents.app import BergAgentsApp
from my_package.agents.custom_reviewer import CustomReviewer

app = BergAgentsApp.create()
app.register_agent("custom_reviewer", CustomReviewer())
```

Registered agents appear in `/agents` (TUI) and `GET /api/agents` (web).

## 3. Run a task through it

```python
result = app.execute(
    "Review the login flow for obvious issues", task_type="generic"
)
print(result)
```

`execute(description, task_type)` returns the harness result dict, including the selected agent, the model used, and any
HITL decision if a pause occurred.
Learning stats: `app.get_router_stats()`.

## Notes

- `preferred_complexity` should match a level in your `model_routing` config (`trivial`, `standard`, `complex`,
  `critical`); per-agent tuning also lives under the `agents` key in `bergagents.jsonc`.
- Keep the change to one logical piece: new file, registration, test, docs.
  See [CONTRIBUTING](../CONTRIBUTING.qmd).
